PrsLangCourseUnit.title: Unit 13: Por vs. Para & Storytelling Past Tenses
PrsLangCourseUnit.name: Por vs. Para & Storytelling Past Tenses
PrsLangCourseUnit.communicativeGoal: Narrate past travel itineraries accurately using preterite vs. imperfect and distinguish por (duration/route) from para (destination/deadline).
PrsLangCourseUnit.grammarGuideMarkdown:
### *Por* vs. *Para* for Duration, Route & Deadlines
- **Duration & Approximate Time:** Use **por** or **durante** (*Viajé por Madrid durante dos semanas*), never *para*.
- **Deadlines & Destinations:** Use **para** (*El informe es para el viernes*; *Salimos para Sevilla*).
- **Preterite vs. Imperfect:** Use preterite for bounded events (*llegué*) and imperfect for background context (*llovía de madrugada*).
PrsLangCourseUnit.operationalSummary: Active B1 focus unit grounding Explain My Answer grammar notes for por/durante vs. para.
PrsLangCourseUnit.invariantRule: GLOBAL_PUBLISHED read-only catalog; grounds Explain My Answer citations.

PrsLangCourseUnit.title: Unit 14: Subjunctive Mood for Advice & Opinions
PrsLangCourseUnit.name: Subjunctive Mood for Advice & Opinions
PrsLangCourseUnit.communicativeGoal: Express recommendations, hopes, and polite doubts in everyday conversations using present subjunctive triggers.
PrsLangCourseUnit.grammarGuideMarkdown:
### Present Subjunctive Triggers
- After **Espero que...**, **Te recomiendo que...**, or **Es mejor que...**, switch vowel endings (`-ar -> -e`, `-er/-ir -> -a`).
- Example: *Espero que **tengas** buen viaje* (not *tienes*).
PrsLangCourseUnit.operationalSummary: Next unlocked B1 unit introducing present subjunctive triggers for advice and opinions.
PrsLangCourseUnit.invariantRule: GLOBAL_PUBLISHED read-only catalog; zero learner PII.

PrsLangCourseUnit.grammarGuideMarkdown:
### Concessive Clauses (*Aunque* / *A pesar de que*)
- Indicative states known facts (*Aunque llueve, salimos*); subjunctive frames hypotheticals (*Aunque llueva mañana, iremos*).
